cards.task: Whenever the ball is out of the way of the door, you must be holding the key at that moment or pick it up afterwards.

wrong.why: Does nothing: the ball starts away from the door, so the rule is triggered at the first step and the key is never taken.
Takes the key, puts it down again and waits: at the end the ball is out of the way and the key is not in hand.
Moves the ball, then waits and never takes the key.

paraphrases: At every moment the ball is out of the way of the door, you have to be carrying the key then, or pick it up later.
If the ball has been moved away from the door, you must be holding the key at that point or at some later point.
Any time the ball is away from the door, the key must be in your hands at that moment or afterwards.
cards.notes: Forced version of `tpl-response-1-nogoal`: the same task, clause and paraphrases, in an environment where the ball starts away from the door (`blocker_moved` is true at the first step). The original passes by doing nothing as long as the agent never moves the ball (seed 1: no-RM judged 1.00, non-empty 0.00); here the rule is triggered at the first step, so doing nothing fails it and the agent must take the key. The solving plan only takes the key: the ball needs no move.

cards.task: If you pick up the key, you must also open the door.

wrong.why: Does nothing: the agent starts holding the key, so the rule is triggered at the first step and the door is never opened.
Walks to the door, keeps the key and waits: the door is never opened.

paraphrases: If you take the key, you also have to open the door.
Taking the key means you must open the door too.
You must open the door if you pick up the key.
cards.notes: Forced version of `tpl-responded-existence-1-nogoal`: the same task, clause and paraphrases, in an environment where the agent starts holding the key (`has_door_key` is true at the first step; `drop` does nothing on the first step). The original passes by doing nothing as long as the agent never takes the key (seed 1: no-RM judged 1.00, non-empty 0.00); here the rule is triggered at the first step, so doing nothing fails it and the agent must open the door. The solving plan only opens the door: the key needs no pickup.
